propositions: Jira-family-general units (identity convention, probe classifier, field sanitizers, link vocabulary, value maps) are scattered across adapters/jira/ and privately imported by sibling adapters, violating the seam contract that requires one-level-deep import edges (core ⇄ adapter only).

The local-to-Jira status and priority maps exist in two independently-referenced copies in jira_fields.py and outbound_fields.py with drift (deleted key missing from jira_fields), creating a single-dict-literal violation.

Relocating jira_fields.py wholesale would invert the dependency direction by making jira_family/ import pinned modules (adf.py, comment_limits.py), so the move must split by symbol: pure logic moves outright, vendor-dependent logic moves parameterized (with codec and limit contracts injected).

Four pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py, identity.py in original scope) are loaded via spec_from_file_location and cannot change paths without breaking the dynamic loader; dependency inversion not relocation must be the sharing strategy.

Absolute imports (not relative) must be used when pinned modules import from jira_family/ because those modules are loaded under synthetic names with no package context, causing relative imports to raise ImportError.

The unified status map must adopt deleted→Done (matching outbound_fields and config.py), fixing the ACLI path's latent bug where deleted tickets would emit the invalid Jira state 'Deleted' instead of a valid workflow transition.
